changes.after: Test values at and just beyond a rule's edges. These checks can catch mistakes after an edit.

before: A regression test records behavior that should remain correct after edits. clamp caps values to 0 through 10. Test below, at, inside and above the range rather than only one ordinary input.

These explicit comparisons return a nonzero process status when any expectation fails. puts announces success only after all checks pass. The changed fixture intentionally weakens the upper cap to expose a boundary regression without running undefined behavior.
Expected output or behavior: checks passed. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add an extreme but valid int input without doing arithmetic that can overflow. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: To clamp a number means keep it within a range by limiting values outside it. This clamp allows 0 through 10. A boundary is an edge of that range. Test below, at, inside, and above the edges.

A regression is a mistake introduced into behavior that used to work. A regression test keeps an expected result so later edits can be checked. This program prints success only if all its comparisons pass.
The tests check -1, 0, 7, 10, and 11. The original clamp handles them correctly, so the program prints checks passed and returns status 0.
Change the upper condition to `n > 11`. An input of 11 then slips through unchanged. The test still expects 10, so it detects the mistake.
